stops.teaser: A tiny studio where Elvis, Johnny Cash and others got their start.

stops.clue: Find the small corner building on Union Avenue with the bright yellow-and-black sign.
stops.safety: Union Avenue is a busy road. Use crosswalks. Tours need tickets, and the studio is still in use.

story: Sam Phillips opened Sun Studio on January 3, 1950, as the Memphis Recording Service, at 706 Union Avenue.

Elvis Presley recorded there in 1953 and 1954. Johnny Cash, Carl Perkins, Jerry Lee Lewis, Howlin' Wolf and B.B. King also recorded there. Jackie Brenston and his Delta Cats recorded Rocket 88 there in 1951, often cited as the first rock and roll single.

On December 4, 1956, Presley, Lewis, Perkins and Cash had an impromptu session that was later called the Million Dollar Quartet. Sun Studio became a National Historic Landmark on July 31, 2003 and is still used by recording artists.
stops.fact: Sam Phillips opened the studio on January 3, 1950.
stops.disputed: "First rock and roll record" is an old argument. Wikipedia calls the Rocket 88 claim reputed.

claims.t: Sam Phillips opened Sun Studio in 1950.
Rocket 88 is certainly the first rock and roll record.
claims.why: It is often cited as the first, but that claim is disputed.

spot.q: The 1937 photo shows Union Avenue before Sun Studio existed. Sun opened on January 3, 1950, and Elvis Presley recorded there in 1953. How many years after it opened was that?
spot.why: The studio opened in 1950 and Elvis recorded there in 1953, three years later.

story: Developer Robertson Topp laid out Beale Street in 1841. It was first called Beale Avenue and was later renamed for Edward Fitzgerald Beale.
W.C. Handy came to Memphis around 1903. He wrote Mr. Crump in 1909 as a campaign song, and it was later renamed The Memphis Blues.

The street declined in the 1960s as urban renewal tore down buildings. Beale Street became a National Historic Landmark in May 1966, and on December 15, 1977, Congress declared it the Home of the Blues.
stops.fact: B.B. King was billed as the Beale Street Blues Boy.
stops.disputed: The Wikipedia article does not use the title Father of the Blues for Handy. Check that nickname before repeating it.

claims.t: Congress declared Beale Street the Home of the Blues in 1977.
Beale Street was built in the 1960s.
claims.why: It was laid out in 1841. The 1960s was a period of decline.

spot.q: Robertson Topp laid out Beale Street in 1841, and Congress declared it the Home of the Blues in 1977. About how many years apart is that?

stops.clue: Go south of downtown on Elvis Presley Boulevard and look for the white mansion behind a wrought-iron gate.

story: Ruth and Thomas Moore built the house in 1939 and named it for Grace Toof, a family relative. Elvis Presley bought it on March 19, 1957 for $102,500.
Elvis died at Graceland on August 16, 1977. His grave is in the Meditation Garden next to the mansion. The Jungle Room has an indoor waterfall and was a recording studio in 1976.
Graceland opened to the public on June 7, 1982. It was listed on the National Register on November 7, 1991 and became a National Historic Landmark on March 27, 2006. The house has 17,552 square feet.
stops.fact: The wrought-iron gate was designed by Abe Sauer.
stops.disputed: The house name comes from Grace Toof, daughter of the founder of a family business, not from the Moores themselves.

claims.t: Graceland opened to the public in 1960.

spot.q: Ruth and Thomas Moore built Graceland in 1939, and Elvis bought it in 1957. How many years had the house stood by then?

stops.name: Memphis Cotton Exchange
stops.teaser: Where fortunes were made on cotton, until trading went digital in 1978.
stops.map: Cotton Exchange Building, 65 Union Ave, Memphis, TN
stops.clue: Go downtown to the corner of Front Street and Union Avenue and find the old exchange building.

story: The Memphis Cotton Exchange was founded in 1874, after the Civil War. It operated as a spot market, where cotton was bought and sold for immediate delivery.
The Cotton Exchange Building stands at the corner of Front Street and Union Avenue. Trading took place on the first floor, where only exchange members could trade.
Floor trading ended in 1978, when computer trading took over. The remodeled historic trading floor is now home to The Cotton Museum.
stops.fact: Only exchange members could trade on the floor.
stops.disputed: Wikipedia is inconsistent on the building date. The infobox says 1925 and the text also mentions 1922, so check the museum's own history.

claims.t: The Memphis Cotton Exchange was founded in 1874.
Floor trading at the exchange ended in 1925.
claims.why: 1925 is the likely building date. Floor trading closed in 1978.

spot.q: The Memphis Cotton Exchange was founded in 1874, and floor trading ended in 1978 when computers took over. How many years is that?
